-81.27570,28.61190.name: The IVF Center
-81.27570,28.61190.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Mark P. Trolice, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

72.97800,19.21800.name: Mahyco / Maharashtra Hybrid Seeds
72.97800,19.21800.desc: The Indian seed company that brought Bt cotton to India in partnership with Monsanto, and later developed Bt brinjal — an aubergine blocked by an Indian moratorium in 2010 and subsequently approved in Bangladesh. Bt cotton now covers the great majority of Indian cotton acreage, which makes this one of the largest adoptions of an engineered crop anywhere, and the country where the argument about farmer debt, seed price and suicide has been most bitterly fought. The scale and the dispute both run through this company.

5.12000,52.09000.name: Nutreco / Skretting
5.12000,52.09000.desc: A major producer of animal and fish feed, including feeds using engineered algal oil as a substitute for wild-caught fish oil. It is one of the clearer cases where an engineered input reduces a documented pressure on wild populations, and the product reaches consumers entirely unlabelled because the engineered organism is not in the fish, only in what the fish ate.

-122.08000,37.41900.desc: Automated mass-rearing and release of sterile mosquitoes, built by a technology company rather than an entomology institute. When releasing tens of millions of insects becomes a logistics problem rather than a biological one, the remaining constraint is permission — and permission systems were written when rearing capacity was the practical brake.

4.83330,45.73330.name: Boehringer Ingelheim — RABORAL V-RG production
4.83330,45.73330.state: Lyon — Boehringer Ingelheim Animal Health, 29 Avenue Tony Garnier
4.83330,45.73330.desc: An engineered virus scattered across landscapes by aircraft, by the hundred million. RABORAL V-RG is an attenuated vaccinia virus carrying the rabies glycoprotein gene, packed in fishmeal-coated sachets and dropped into wildlife habitat for foxes, raccoons, coyotes and jackals to eat. It has been in continuous use since it was first field tested in foxes in Belgium in 1987, and roughly 250 million doses have been distributed worldwide since. It is one of two oral bait vaccines the World Health Organization recommends for wildlife rabies control, and its field use has been credited with eliminating wildlife rabies from Belgium, France and Luxembourg and the dog and coyote rabies variant from the United States. It is also the largest deliberate environmental release of an engineered organism anywhere on this map, and it is a public health programme rather than a commercial planting — which is exactly why it belongs here. The category of release is not defined by whether the purpose is good.
